t: A northern British kingdom formed from the Picts and Gaelic Dál Riata, traditionally dated to Kenneth MacAlpin around 843.
It kept its independence against England in the Wars of Independence, won by Robert the Bruce at Bannockburn in 1314.
James VI inherited England in 1603, and the Acts of Union of 1707 merged the two kingdoms into Great Britain.
dyk: James II of Scotland, an enthusiast for artillery, was killed in 1460 when one of his own cannons burst during the siege of Roxburgh Castle.
ev: Kenneth MacAlpin becomes king of the Picts
The Treaty of Perth transfers the Western Isles from Norway
Robert the Bruce defeats Edward II at Bannockburn
The Declaration of Arbroath asserts Scottish independence
James IV is killed at the Battle of Flodden
The Reformation Parliament creates a Protestant church
James VI inherits the English throne
The Acts of Union create the Kingdom of Great Britain

f.capital: Scone and other royal centres; later Edinburgh
f.predecessor: Kingdom of the Picts; Dál Riata
